New Delhi is the capital city the British built for their Indian empire just south of old Delhi, announced in 1911 and opened in 1931. It is now the seat of India's government.

At the Delhi Durbar of December 1911, King George V announced that the capital would move from Calcutta to Delhi, the old seat of the Mughals and sultans. The architects Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker laid out a city of wide avenues, roundabouts and gardens on Raisina Hill.

Its main buildings form one long axis:

  • The Viceroy's House, now Rashtrapati Bhavan, the president's home, under a dome modelled partly on Buddhist stupas.
  • Two Secretariat blocks by Baker, and a round council house that became Parliament.
  • A great avenue, then called Kingsway, running to India Gate, a memorial to Indian soldiers of the First World War.

The style blends European classical forms with Indian details such as stone screens and small domed pavilions. Sixteen years later it became the capital of independent India, set beside the older Mughal city of Shahjahanabad.
sum: New Delhi is the capital city the British built for their Indian empire just south of old Delhi, announced in 1911 and opened in 1931. It is now the seat of India's government.
